newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka spot rates flat, speculators buy forwards.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka spot rates flat, speculators buy forwards.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed barely moved on Monday on limited commercial demand for dollars, while activity was focussed on forward rates, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.79 to the dollar after opening at 57.78. The rupee closed at 57.77 on Friday.
"The dollar went to 57.83 rupees on a little import covering but soon fell back due to selling," said a Citibank dealer.
Activity was centred around one and three-month forward contracts since banks believe any short-term movement of the exchange rate was unlikely, he said.

Some dealers however, say it is not likely that the exchange rate would move aggressively in either direction even in the longer term, since the Central Bank has clearly demonstrated its commitment to a stable and low rate regime.
Overnight call money rates closed at 11.75 percent after opening at 13 percent, dealers said.
"Money is well offered and if no one builds dollar positions either, call rates are going to remain low," said a Panasia Bank dealer.
